title: DMV-Bench: Diagnosing Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents' Visual Memory with Incidental Cue Injection
abstract: arXiv:2606.27499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agent benchmarks for measuring memory largely study textual cases, in which information is deliberately extracted from the environment, written down, and then later retrieved. In other words, they assess what agents elected to record, not what they happened to see. We introduce DMV-Bench (code: https://github.com/yyyujintang/DMV-Bench), the first interactive benchmark for visual memory in multimodal agents, to study this often-neglected property. DMV-Bench is built on (1) a controlled home-furnishing e-commerce environment, supported by a catalog of 1,000 product variants, and (2) a text-leakage contract which ensures that the primary discriminative signal of each task is solely in the pixels. In DMV-Bench, agents undergo chains of autonomous shopping sessions in which every visited product image carries a unique, pre-rendered incidental cue that the agent is later asked to recall. translated_title: DMV-Bench：通过偶然线索注入诊断长程多模态智能体的视觉记忆
translated_abstract: 用于衡量记忆的智能体基准大多研究文本案例，即信息被有意地从环境中提取、记录下来，之后再被检索。换言之，它们评估的是智能体选择记录的内容，而非它们偶然看到的内容。我们提出DMV-Bench（代码：https://github.com/yyyujintang/DMV-Bench），这是首个针对多模态智能体视觉记忆的交互式基准，用以研究这一常被忽视的特性。DMV-Bench建立在（1）一个受控的家居用品电商环境之上，该环境由包含1,000种产品变体的目录支持；（2）一条文本泄露契约，确保每个任务的主要判别信号仅存在于像素之中。在DMV-Bench中，智能体经历一系列自主购物会话，其中每个被访问的产品图像都携带一个独特的、预先渲染的偶然线索，智能体随后被要求回忆这些线索。我们表明，传统方案难以……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: DMV-Bench是首个评估多模态智能体视觉记忆的交互式基准，它通过在自主购物会话中向产品图像注入独特的偶然线索，并确保任务判别信号仅存在于像素中，来诊断长程智能体对偶然所见视觉信息的记忆能力。
en_tdlr: DMV-Bench is the first interactive benchmark for multimodal agents' visual memory, which injects unique incidental cues into product images during autonomous shopping sessions and ensures task-discriminative signals reside solely in pixels, to diagnose long-horizon agents' memory of incidentally seen visual information.
